title: POC scoping: cost modeling with Elyra Analytics
next_steps: Samir to send modeled pricing spreadsheet and committed-use options (by 2026-08-14)
Jia to propose benchmark test cases and sample prompts (by 2026-08-17)
Elyra to provide representative prompt set and traffic profile (by 2026-08-18)
Schedule kickoff benchmark run (30-45 min) w/ infra team (target week of 2026-08-24)
action_items: Samir (Redwood AE) - send pricing spreadsheet + example contract language - due 2026-08-14
Jia (Redwood SE) - share benchmark harness + initial runbook for latency/throughput tests - due 2026-08-17

summary: Initial POC scoping to align on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, and cost model. Main concerns: per-token unit economics, batching/caching knobs, dedicated vs hosted cost tradeoffs, and a 3-week timeline for an initial benchmark. Next steps include sharing prompt set, pricing sheet, and scheduling benchmark run.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro - I'm Samir, AE on the Redwood inference team. Jia (SE) and I will run through how we typically scope POCs for cost modeling. Uh, first, can folks introduce themselves?
[00:12] Maya (Elyra): Maya here, Head of ML. We've got a couple use cases: real-time summarization for analyst dashboards and nightly batch reranks.
[00:20] Carlos (Elyra): Carlos, CTO. Budget is the big gating factor; we need to understand unit economics before committing to dedicated capacity.
[00:28] Leah (Elyra): Leah, platform eng - I'll own the infra side for the POC.
[00:31] Oliver (Elyra): Oliver, procurement - just here to note contracting timeline constraints.
[00:35] Jia (Redwood SE): Great, thanks. Quick agenda: we want to align on success criteria, sample workload size, benchmarks to run, and then walk through our cost model assumptions - per-token, batching, caching, and quantization impacts.
[00:50] Samir: Before we dive in - do you prefer Redwood hosted API for the POC or a private/VPC deploy? That will change pricing assumptions a bit.
[00:58] Maya: For the POC, hosted is fine, we just want to validate economics. If results look good we'll evaluate dedicated or private.
[01:05] Carlos: Hosted works as long as we can measure latencies and see consistent cost estimates. We have some regulatory constraints but not strict yet.
[01:12] Jia: Cool. On success criteria - typical ones are: end-to-end 95th percentile latency under X ms for real-time flows, cost per call under $Y, and quality (fidelity) delta vs baseline less than Z. For Elyra, do you have target numbers?
[01:30] Maya: Latency target is 250ms p95 for the live summarization; cost target is roughly $0.003 per call, but that depends on how we define a call (tokens). For batch reranks, throughput and per-record cost matter more.
[01:44] Samir: Okay, helpful. We'll map that to per-token numbers. Two notes: 1) per-token cost varies by model and quantization; 2) operational savings from batching and prefix/KV caching can be material for nighttime batch jobs.
[02:02] Jia: Let's go through a quick worked example. If your average prompt+response is 150 tokens and we assume a 32K-ish model, raw hosted price might be around $0.00002 per input token and $0.00006 per output token at list - rough numbers - but with batching and efficient runtime we often cut the effective unit cost by 20-60% depending on cache hit rate.
[02:25] Carlos: Those numbers seem low - can you show the spreadsheet?
[02:28] Samir: I'll send the modeled spreadsheet after. Note those are illustrative; we'll compute exact per-token below once we have prompt distribution.
[02:36] Maya: Two important factors for Elyra: our prompts are relatively long in context for summaries - about 600 tokens average context + 120 token answer. So token counts are higher.
[02:45] Jia: That shifts cost; also KV cache helps if many requests share prefixes, e.g., same document bodies for multiple queries - though for fresh summaries cache hits are lower.
[02:55] Leah: For the batch rerank job, we can do heavy batching - jobs run overnight, thousands of records, so per-token effective cost will be much lower.
[03:03] Samir: Exactly. We'll model two workload profiles: real-time (low-latency, small batches, minimal cache) and batch (high-throughput, large batch sizes, caching opportunities).
[03:15] Jia: Regarding benchmarking - we'll run: single-request p95 latency tests, sustained throughput tests (samples/sec), and cost-per-1M-token projections. We'll provide the harness - it's a lightweight runner that can simulate concurrency and batching.
[03:30] Carlos: How do you handle model fallbacks? If a large model is costly, can we automatically route to a smaller one for some traffic?
[03:36] Samir: Yes, smart routing is in the platform - can do A/B to split by route or do automatic fallback to quantized variants. For cost modeling we include fallback mixes as scenarios.
[03:45] Maya: We care about quality regressions. How will you measure fidelity? We'll want a small eval set of golden outputs.
[03:52] Jia: We'll run quality checks using your golden prompts and compute similarity/diff metrics - can integrate evaluation into the benchmark harness and alert to any regression beyond agreed threshold.
[04:00] Oliver: Contract/timeline side - procurement needs to see estimated monthly cost for projected 6-month usage. What's the POC timeline?
[04:07] Samir: Typical POC is 3 weeks: week 1 collect prompts and run baseline local tests; week 2 run hosted benchmarks and tuning; week 3 analyze and present results + pricing. We can compress if Elyra provides prompts quickly.
[04:20] Carlos: That works. Are there hardware or VPC requirements for hosted tests?
[04:25] Leah: We can route from our VPC to hosted endpoints if needed; otherwise we'll use public endpoints for initial runs.
[04:31] Jia: For the cost model I want to call out knobs: batching size, batching delay (latency budget), KV/prefix cache hit rate, model size/quantization (int8 vs int4), and request routing (dedicated reserved vs on-demand). We'll produce scenario tables.
[04:47] Maya: Can you give a quick sense of the delta between hosted and dedicated? Ballpark numbers are fine.
[04:52] Samir: Ballpark: if you commit to dedicated capacity with reserved monthly commit, you might see 30-50% lower per-token compute cost at scale depending on utilization. But there's a base infra commitment and amortization. For low-volume or bursty workloads hosted is often cheaper short-term.
[05:10] Carlos: Ok, good. For our budgeting we need a modeled example: 1M realtime calls per month at 150 tokens call average, plus 50M batch tokens monthly.
[05:20] Jia: We'll model that. Quick arithmetic: 1M * 150 = 150M tokens realtime; plus 50M batch = 200M tokens total. Then apply model-specific input/output splits. We'll show scenarios with and without caching, and with quantized model variants.
[05:35] Maya: Also include cost of observability retention - we need logs for audits. Does Redwood charge extra for longer retention?
[05:42] Samir: Yes, advanced observability add-ons are extra. We'll include that as a line item (e.g., 30-day vs 90-day retention). We'll note SOC2/ISO docs too.
[05:52] Oliver: On security - we'll need SOC2 Type II, audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC. Any gotchas for hosted?
[05:59] Jia: Hosted supports SSO/SAML and RBAC; we can provide SOC2 report and audit log samples. For stricter requirements, Private (VPC/on-prem) is available but increases time and cost. We'll attach security pack.
[06:12] Maya: For the benchmark harness - will it emulate prefix reuse for the batch job? We actually have cases where we feed slightly different queries over the same documents.
[06:20] Jia: Yes, we can configure prefix similarity and cache hit rates. We'll want a small set of representative document templates to simulate realistic cache behavior.
[06:30] Samir: I'm going to sketch the cost model rows we'll send: compute per-token, storage for KV cache impact, network egress (if cross-region), observability costs, reserved commit amortization, and any per-request overheads like increased latency costs for small payloads.
[06:46] Carlos: What about quantization quality? If we go int8 or int4 to save cost, will we lose too much accuracy for our summarization?
[06:52] Jia: It depends on model architecture and the task. We'll run a quantization sweep in the POC to measure delta on your eval set. Often int8 is near-transparent; int4 can introduce regressions on edge cases. We'll report per-scenario quality metrics.
[07:10] Maya: Good. Also curious about batching latency trade-offs - if we batch to 8 requests we may save 20% cost but increase tail latency; can you model that?
[07:18] Samir: Yes we'll include latency vs cost curve for batching sizes. We'll flag operating points that meet your p95 requirement.
[07:25] Leah: For batch rerank - can you support GPU-accelerated batching? We run on-prem nightly but could run on Redwood Dedicated for comparison.
[07:33] Jia: Absolutely, Dedicated supports GPU pools and continuous batching KVs. For the POC we can simulate dedicated by running sustained throughput tests on hosted and then extrapolate to dedicated pricing.
[07:45] Samir: We'll attach an example pricing table in the spreadsheet: columns for model type, quantization, batching assumptions, effective per-token compute price, monthly cost for projected tokens, and recommended operating mode.
[07:58] Oliver: Procurement note: we need an MSA and terms for a short 3-month pilot. Can you send standard MSA?
[08:05] Samir: Yes, I'll include a draft MSA and sample SOW for the POC.
[08:10] Maya: One last question on benchmarks: what kind of noise should we expect in measurements? We want to be confident in p95s.
[08:16] Jia: We'll run repeated trials at different times and provide confidence intervals. For hosted tests, there is some variability; we'll run enough samples to be +/- 5% on p95 typically.
[08:28] Carlos: Great. Let's talk slightly more concrete numbers - show me one worked scenario using your default medium model.
[08:34] Samir: Okay - hypothetical: medium LLM, non-quantized, hosted list compute cost say $X per token (we'll put exact in sheet) - for your 200M tokens we might land at $A/month. If we enable batching for 80% of batch tokens and get 30% effective saving, and cache reduces some prefix cost for 10% of realtime, we can show a reduced total. Jia will produce three scenarios: conservative, expected, optimistic.
[09:02] Jia: I'll also create a sensitivity table showing per-token cost vs batch size and cache hit rate.
[09:08] Maya: That will be super helpful. For success criteria let's lock: p95 <= 250ms for live flow, model quality within 2% of current baseline on golden set, and total monthly cost under $X (we'll confirm $X after you produce scenarios).
[09:24] Samir: Sounds good. Quick operational questions: will you want to enable function/tool calling or structured outputs in the POC? That can affect token counts.
[09:32] Maya: We'll include structured JSON outputs for the analyst dashboard - expect slightly longer outputs.
[09:36] Jia: Noted. We'll bump output token estimate accordingly.
[09:40] Samir: Anything else on security or compliance?
[09:43] Oliver: Please include data retention and deletion guarantees in the docs.
[09:46] Samir: Will do. We'll include KMS/HSM options for private deployments too.
[09:50] Jia: On timelines - once we receive prompts and traffic profile (Maya/Carlos), we'll schedule benchmark runs. Expect first-run results within 7-10 business days.
[09:59] Maya: We'll share prompts by end of week.
[10:02] Samir: Great. I'll recap next steps at the end and drop the spreadsheet after the call.
[10:06] [-- brief pause --]
[10:25] Samir: Okay quick recap: 1) Elyra shares prompts + traffic histogram; 2) Redwood shares pricing spreadsheet, benchmark harness, and MSA draft; 3) Redwood runs hosted benchmarks (latency/throughput/quantization sweep) and returns results; 4) decide on follow-up (dedicated pilot or continued hosted).
[10:48] Maya: That matches our expectations. Procurement will review MSA.
[11:00] Oliver: We'll try to get decisions on hosted vs dedicated budget by 2026-08-21.
[11:10] Samir: Perfect. Anything else before we close?
[11:14] Carlos: One small thing - include network egress assumptions in the sheet, we're multi-region.
[11:19] Jia: Will do, we'll include cross-region egress and show sensitivity.
[11:25] Samir: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with artifacts.
[54:50] [call ends]

Notes: transcription has occasional mislabels and filler words; references to docs: pricing spreadsheet (link sent post-call), benchmark harness (github link provided by Jia), security pack (SOC2) will be attached. This transcript is lightly edited for readability but intentionally keeps filler and some misrecognitions (e.g., Redwood Optimise, int four vs in four) to mimic automated transcription quirks.
